authoredPrompt: This figure contains two panels (a and b), each showing a diagram of a shallow neural network with one input node x, three hidden units h_1, h_2, h_3, and one output node y. In panel (b), two bias nodes labeled 1 are present — one feeding the hidden layer and one feeding the output — and the connections from hidden units to the output are labeled with weights φ_1, φ_2, φ_3 plus a bias weight φ_0; a single representative input-to-hidden weight θ_{11} is also labeled to indicate the notation convention. In panel (a), the weight labeling emphasizes the hidden-layer side: the bias connections to each hidden unit carry weights θ_{10}, θ_{20}, θ_{30}, and the connections from input x carry weights θ_{21} and θ_{31}, making the full first-layer parameterization explicit. Arrows in both panels use black and orange coloring to distinguish the input-side (pre-activation) connections from the output-side (post-activation) connections. This figure introduces the standard parameterization of a shallow network, showing how θ weights govern the input-to-hidden linear transformation and φ weights govern the hidden-to-output linear combination.
authoredInteractions:
- Click a hidden neuron h_i to highlight its incoming weight from x and bias, plus its outgoing contribution to output y, making the weight labels φ_i and θ_ij visible
- Toggle between panels a and b to compare the clean network diagram with the fully labeled weight view showing all φ and θ parameter names
- Slider for number of hidden units: add or remove neurons from the hidden layer while keeping the single input x and output y fixed

discrepancies: The base mathematical characters (θ, φ, h) are completely missing from all nodes and edge labels; only their numerical subscripts are visible.
The cyan ReLU activation symbol in the hidden nodes is shifted to the right, whereas it passes directly through the center in the source.
The edge labels (e.g., θ₁₀, φ₁) are placed in rigid vertical columns rather than aligning with and floating alongside their respective edges as in the source.
evaluation.notes: The interactive translation is conceptually excellent with great pedagogical features, but a rendering bug in the multi-part text labels swallows all the base variables (θ, φ, h), severely damaging the mathematical readability of the figure.
action_items: Fix the drawMathLabelWithHalo text rendering: calling .cx().cy() on text elements with multiple tspans can break SVG bounding-box calculations. Apply .attr({x: cx, y: cy}) directly to the text element with 'anchor: middle'.
Adjust the coordinates of the cyan ReLU polyline in drawReLU so it is centered inside the hidden node circles.
Position the edge labels along the visual midpoint of their respective edges rather than clamping them to a single vertical column.
